{{Quote|That speeder is one of my most prized possessions.|Simon Greyshade|<ref name="HNN" />}}
The '''XJ-6 airspeeder''' was a custom-built [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeder]] fashioned to [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Simon Greyshade/Legends|Simon Greyshade's]] elitist and performance-driven tastes. Using a [[Narglatch AirTech prefabricated kit|prefabricated kit]] produced by [[Narglatch AirTech/Legends|Narglatch AirTech]], the senator's personal [[Technician/Legends|mechanics]] designed and built the custom airspeeder. The XJ-6 was constructed with [[Condensed-matter composite|exotic materials]] and incorporated advanced systems into its design, including an [[Acceleration compensator/Legends|inertial compensator]]&mdash;typically only used in [[Realspace/Legends|space-bound]] [[Starship/Legends|craft]]. Two prominent, oversized [[Turbofan/Legends|turbofan]] [[Seventh-stage bank-courier repulsor-truck engine|engines]] at the fore of the craft provided immense power to the XJ-6, and an [[electrogravitic gyro flywheel]] allowed the craft to make abrupt turns without requiring traction. The souped-up speeder also sported a custom [[Color/Legends|yellow]] paint job. Greyshade used the speeder both as a luxury [[Transport/Legends|transport]] as well as a racing vehicle in [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant's]] airspeeder races.

The airspeeder gained attention in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] after its apparent [[Thief/Legends|theft]] outside of the [[Senate apartment complex/Legends|Senate Apartment Complex]]. [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] appropriated the speeder to rescue his [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], as the latter plummeted through the Coruscant [[Skylane/Legends|skylanes]]. Once Kenobi was saved, the two Jedi took turns [[Pilot/Legends|piloting]] the XJ-6 airspeeder as they pursued the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]] through the [[City/Legends|cityscape]] following her failed [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]] [[Plot to assassinate Senator Amidala/Legends|attempt]] on Senator [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]]. After the chase had ended, Coruscant authorities tracked the XJ-6 to [[Vos Gesal Street/Legends|Vos Gesal Street]], over a hundred [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] from its original parking spot in the [[Senate District/Legends|Senate District]]. [[Reymet Autem]], son of a [[Sagoro Autem|Senate Guard]] who worked with Greyshade, was initially charged with the theft, but the airspeeder was clandestinely returned to its spot in the lot of [[500 Republica/Legends|500 Republica]] before charges could be filed. The authorities never discovered the true thief, much to Greyshade's disdain, and he vowed to find the party responsible.

==Description==
===Built for sport===
{{Quote|It took my mechanics years to perfect it.|Simon Greyshade|<ref name="HNN" />}}
[[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Simon Greyshade/Legends|Simon Greyshade]] commissioned his [[Technician/Legends|mechanics]]<ref name="AotC:ICS" /> to build a hot-rod [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeder]] using a [[Narglatch AirTech prefabricated kit|prefabricated kit]] produced by [[Narglatch AirTech/Legends|Narglatch AirTech]].<ref name="NewFF64" /> The resulting open-top, designated as an XJ-6 airspeeder<ref name="NEGtVaV" /> and wholly unique to other vehicles, took Greyshade's mechanics [[Standard year/Legends|years]] to design and build<ref name="HNN" /> and contained several features intended to show off the senator's passions for both speed and luxury. The airspeeder was flown by a lone [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]], with the design including a secondary passenger seat situated beside the pilot's. This catered to the senator's desire for privacy while escorting others, ranging from fellow senators and influential [[Politics/Legends|politicians]] to his latest female companion.<ref name="AotC:ICS" /> The design of the aircraft itself was similar to [[Simon Greyshade's B69 Elektra airspeeder|Greyshade's B69 Elektra airspeeder]],<ref name="VivaSpaceVegas">{{SW|url=news/viva-space-vegas-the-history-of-the-marvelous-wheel-part-2|series=Viva Space Vegas! The History of the Marvelous Wheel|text=Part 2|nolive=1}}</ref> including the structure and placement of the forward-mounted [[Engine/Legends|engines]].<ref name="Honor and Duty">[[Republic 47|''Republic'' 47]]</ref>

[[File:XJ6Diagram-FF029.png|thumb|left|270px|A diagram of the XJ-6 airspeeder]]
Exotic metal alloys, [[condensed-matter composite]], and a number of other metals made up the main body of the craft, which measured 6.23 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] long, 2.66 meters wide, and 1.4 meters tall. The front bumper was specifically designed to distribute forces evenly across the craft to prevent any harmful structure vibrations. Due to this structural composition, the XJ-6 had a relatively low mass&mdash;1,600 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]]&mdash;which allowed it to move quickly and reliably maintain the momentum that the massive engines created.<ref name="AotC:ICS" />

[[Electrogravitic gyro flywheel]]s located toward the rear of the XJ-6 airspeeder allowed the craft impressive feats of maneuvering at sharp angles uncommon to air vehicles of its class.<ref name="NEGtVaV" /> These flywheels also allowed the XJ-6 airspeeder to turn without traction or aerodynamic influence.<ref name="AotC:ICS" /> A pair of flaps, located on the underside of the speeder, assisted in braking and turning.<ref name="AotC" /> An [[Acceleration compensator/Legends|inertial compensator]], generally only found in [[Starship/Legends|space-bound craft]],<ref name="CATCW" /> was utilized to keep pilot and passenger safe from the effects of these harsh maneuvers. Despite the existence of equipment used in spacecraft installed in the XJ-6,<ref name="AotC:ICS" /> it was unable to travel into deep [[Realspace/Legends|space]].<ref name="AOTC schematics book">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: Ship Schematics Punch-Out Book]]''</ref> In addition to the inertial compensator, riders were held in the craft's seats by a pair<ref name="CATCW" /> of [[Tractor beam/Legends|miniature tractor units]].<ref name="AotC:ICS" />

The speeder's exterior was dominated by the over-scaled engines in the craft's fore as well as the striking curves in the [[Hull/Legends|hull]] design of the aft compartment. Two running boards, one on each side of the airspeeder, spanned the distance from the fore engine bay to the seats located in the midsection of the craft. Between the engines and the [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]], a sloped [[Hull/Legends|hull]] section contained the ship's steering controls and thruster ducts and was topped by a short windscreen. The airspeeder's engine exhausts and electrogravitic gyro flywheel assemblies were concealed by the curvaceous nature of the rear hull section. Headrests for the vehicle's occupants were built into the aft hull, each respectively located just above the top of the speeder's two seats. The sweeping underside of the XJ-6 featured two thin, ridged strips, [[Color/Legends|colored]] gray, running parallel from the fore to the aft of the airspeeder.<ref name="AotC" />

The airspeeder was painted yellow,<ref name="AotC" /> the color customary to all of the senator's vehicles.<ref name="FF29" /> Both Greyshade and [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]]<ref name="JuniorAotC">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones'' junior novelization]]</ref> described the speeder's color as "[[List of phrases and slang/Legends#G|gonzo]]."<ref name="HNN" /> Dull green and orange accented the yellow and were scattered throughout the craft's paint scheme, and the airspeeder's interior, including the dual seats, was predominantly dark brown.<ref name="AotC" /> Both rear fins of the craft sported racing stickers, which revealed racing venues Greyshade had visited during his after-[[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] activities.<ref name="NEGtVaV" /><ref name="FF29" />

===Airspeeder amenities===
{{Quote|It's a gonzo color. I won't rest until I've destroyed the life of the sleemo who took it.|Simon Greyshade, upon the recovery of his airspeeder|<ref name="HNN" />}}
[[File:GreyshadeSpeeder-HNNv531no56.png|thumb|right|270px|The XJ-6 airspeeder was painted a "gonzo" yellow.]]
The low profile of the XJ-6's windscreen forced both pilot and passenger to sit low, and a powerful sound system occupied a space on the dashboard for the senator's enjoyment.<ref name="AotC:ICS" /> A set of piloting controls that included a gear selector and two joysticks to control direction sat above the port-side seat,<ref name="FF29" /> and an eight-speed combination thrust control was fixed between the pilot and passenger seats.<ref name="NewFF64" /> [[Comm unit/Legends|Communications gear]] sat behind the driver and passenger, between the two headrests built into the hull. The high-power antennas in the communications suite allowed Greyshade to communicate with fellow lawmakers and other contacts while in the airspeeder.<ref name="AotC:ICS" />

Dual low-beam lights flanking the engines lit the speeder's way, and a combination longer-range widebeam light and collision scanner mounted on the front bumper kept the pilot aware of obstacles in the flight path. An electric field system ensured that oncoming objects, such as flying [[Insect/Legends|insects]] and debris, were repulsed from striking the craft.<ref name="AotC:ICS" /> However, the possibility remained for objects to pass through this field. Items that breached the field posed a risk to the exposed engines.<ref name="FF29" /> In addition, the construction of the XJ-6 airspeeder allowed it to pass through the discharge of two [[Power coupling/Legends|power coupling]] prongs unscathed, though riders were not as well protected. On the rear of the craft, tucked in various places on the shapely rear plating, were a number of red braking lights. These lights illuminated upon the craft's deceleration, indicating to other drivers that the XJ-6 was slowing down.<ref name="AotC" />

The XJ-6 lacked any sort of offensive capability, such as [[Blaster cannon/Legends|blaster cannons]], forcing those piloting the craft to rely on the vehicle's speed and agility in any altercations. To ensure the speeder's protection from [[Thief/Legends|theft]], [[Motion sensor/Legends|movement sensors]] were installed. If they were tripped, an alarm would go off, notifying Greyshade and any bystanders of the illegal action. However, this security system was vulnerable to a technologically-adept thief.<ref name="AotC:ICS" /> A [[Homing beacon/Legends|tracking device]] was built into the speeder in case the craft was ever lost. Described as hyper-accurate, the tracking device allowed [[Coruscanti/Legends|Coruscanti]] [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|authorities]] to locate the speeder a mere thirty [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]] after it had disappeared.<ref name="HNN" />

===Engines===
{{Quote|Oh, you know, Master. I couldn't find a speeder that I really liked, with the open cockpit and the right speed capabilities.|Anakin Skywalker, on appropriating Greyshade's XJ-6 airspeeder|<ref name="AotC" />}}
[[File:Xj-6_engine_ics.png|thumb|left|270px|The port-side turbofan engine]]
In addition to its distinct paint scheme, the yellow hot-rod airspeeder was also recognizable due to the custom, dual [[Turbofan/Legends|turbofan]] [[Seventh-stage bank-courier repulsor-truck engine|engines]] fitted in the front of the craft. These two engines, running on [[Deuterium/Legends|Deuterium]] [[Fuel/Legends|fuel]]<ref name="AotC" /> and capable of producing thirty [[megawatt]]s of power,<ref name="FF29" /> were originally built to be used in groups of fifty for the colossal [[Seventh-stage bank-courier repulsor-truck/Legends|seventh-stage bank-courier repulsor-trucks]] of [[Aargau/Legends|Aargau]].<ref name="Databank">{{DB|vehicle|anakinsspeeder|airspeeder, Anakin Skywalker's}}</ref> They eventually came into Greyshade's possession, and he had his mechanics install them into the XJ-6 airspeeder and modify the already powerful engines to further utilize their potential. The immense weight of the engines required a dedicated [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] engine.<ref name="AotC:ICS" /> The original cowlings were removed to allow easy modifications, repair, and tweaking.<ref name="FF29" /> A cold-start [[Power generator/Legends|generator]] allowed the XJ-6 to start up almost immediately without the warm-up period standard in vehicles of its class. The oversized engines could reach speeds up to 720 [[Kilometer per hour/Legends|kilometers per hour]] with an acceleration of seventy G and operated much like two [[Podracer/Legends|Podracer]] engines in function and ability due to their stance on the craft.<ref name="SWGalaxies">{{GalaxiesNGE}}</ref> This stance also minimized the craft's width, granting the speeder good clearance for tight maneuvers.<ref name="AotC:ICS" /> The engines were expensive, gaudy, and displayed Greyshade's tastes in expensive and overpowered devices.<ref name="FF29" /> In appearance, the engines were common to another speeder owned by the senator, a customized [[B69 Elektra airspeeder|B69 Elektra]].<ref name="VivaSpaceVegas" /><ref name="Honor and Duty" />

The twin engines functioned by drawing air into the forward turbines, which fed into the compression chambers. This air was over-pressurized due to the exposed turbofans and was then forced through ignitions and narrow ducts situated in the sidewalls and undercarriage of the craft<ref name="FF29" /> at incredible speeds.<ref name="NewFF64" /> The air continued to travel to the rear thrusters after passing through another set of afterburner centrifuges. An internal shutter system acted as a braking mechanism to stop, slow, and precisely maneuver the craft, working in conjunction with the flywheels in the aft of the aircraft.<ref name="AotC:ICS" /> Debris, such as a flag, proved a possible hazard to the engines by dropping the power output,<ref name="AOTCNovel">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' novelization]]</ref> as the turbofan assembly was highly exposed.<ref name="FF29" />

==History==
===The senator's need for speed===
[[File:XJ6speeder.jpg|thumb|right|270px|The senator's XJ-6 airspeeder]]
Simon Greyshade lived on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]<ref name="Honor and Duty" /> by [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]]<ref name="ComicCompanion">''[[Star Wars: The Comics Companion]]''</ref> after replacing his [[Assassin/Legends|assassinated]] [[Jheramahd Greyshade|cousin]] as senator of the [[Vorzyd sector/Legends|Vorzyd sector]] in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]].<ref name="Honor and Duty" /> An airspeeder hobbyist and racing enthusiast, the senator used his position's power and wealth to commission the construction of a luxury personal [[Transport/Legends|transport]] for use while on Coruscant.<ref name="AotC:ICS" /> Using a modification kit produced by Narglatch AirTech,<ref name="Databank" /> Greyshade's personal mechanics took [[Standard month/Legends|months]] to perfect the resulting craft, the XJ-6 airspeeder, to Greyshade's exacting specifications.<ref name="NewFF64" /> Additionally, its coloration, unique to Greyshade's vehicles, had taken years to develop.<ref name="HNN" /> The speeder incorporated an array of exotic metals and components, two oversized engines providing the XJ-6 with incredible power, and a flywheel system responsible for the quick turns and sharp ascents and descents for which the craft's profile called.<ref name="AotC:ICS" /> The mechanics even installed an inertial compensator to shield both pilot and passenger from the craft's harsh maneuvers and blinding speeds.<ref name="CATCW" /> After construction, the speeder was painted Greyshade's customary yellow&mdash;common to all of his vehicles.<ref name="FF29" />

Greyshade used the custom hot rod in after-hours races through the [[City/Legends|cityscape]] of Coruscant with his legislature colleagues. He showed off his prowess with the racing stickers plastered on the rear fins of the craft.<ref name="AotC:ICS" /> In fact, his constant use of the XJ-6 airspeeder convinced fellow senator [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Prestor Organa]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] to purchase and construct the Narglatch Airtech [[XJ-2 airspeeder/Legends|XJ-2 airspeeder]] for personal use.<ref name="BailOrgana">{{DB|vehicle|bailspeeder|airspeeder, Bail Organa's}}</ref> Greyshade often kept the XJ-6 in a speeder dock of the [[Senate apartment complex/Legends|Senate Apartment Complex]], where he held a designated parking spot.<ref name="ItWoAotC">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Attack of the Clones]]''</ref>

===Chase through Coruscant===
{{Quote|Anakin! How many times have I told you&hellip; stay away from power&hellip; couplings?|Obi-Wan Kenobi, to Anakin Skywalker, as the latter pilots the XJ-6 through a pair of discharging power couplings|<ref name="AotC" />}}
[[File:Attack_of_the_clones_1.jpg|thumb|left|270px|Anakin Skywalker pilots the XJ-6 airspeeder as Obi-Wan Kenobi seeks assassin Zam Wesell.]]
Shortly before the outbreak of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Simon Greyshade's airspeeder became an instrumental factor in the pursuit of fugitive [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]], whose [[Plot to assassinate Senator Amidala/Legends|failed attempt]] on the life of Senator [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] prompted investigation. After the discovery of the presence of an [[ASN-121/Legends|ASN-121]] [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]] outside the [[Window/Legends|window]] of [[Naboo Queen (restaurant)|Amidala's apartment]] in the Senate Apartment Complex, [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] attempted to pursue the attacker by grabbing hold of the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] as it exited the premises. Rather than follow his [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] out the window into the Coruscant [[Skylane/Legends|skylanes]],<ref name="AotC" /> Padawan Anakin Skywalker opted to retrieve an airspeeder from a speeder dock located several levels below Amidala's apartment.<ref name="ItWoAotC" /> Assessing the available options, Skywalker chose Greyshade's XJ-6 airspeeder,<ref name="AotC" /> as it was the only convertible speeder on the lot.<ref name="ItWoAotC" /> Using a combination of technical knowledge and [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], Skywalker disabled the security countermeasures installed by Greyshade's mechanics<ref name="AotC:ICS" /> and took off in pursuit of Kenobi, still hanging from the escaping assassin droid.<ref name="AotC" />

Breaking Jedi policies on airship piloting,<ref name="AotCVD" /> Skywalker pushed the craft's engines to catch up to his Master, who was plummeting through the skylanes of [[Galactic City/Legends|Galactic City]], as Wesell had shot the ASN-121 droid in an attempt to lose the Jedi investigator. Skywalker relied on the XJ-6 airspeeder's impressive speed and maneuverability as he placed the craft into a near-vertical dive in order to reach the free-falling Kenobi. Once Kenobi landed safely in the speeder's passenger seat, Skywalker piloted the craft to follow Wesell's [[Koro-2 all-environment exodrive airspeeder|''Koro''-2 airspeeder]].<ref name="AotC" /> The chase grew more intense as the two speeding craft made their respective ways through Coruscant's bustling traffic and maze of buildings, each narrowly evading oncoming vehicles. During the pursuit, Skywalker hit a flag, which caught in one of the engines, but Kenobi removed the object to prevent adverse affects to the speeder.<ref name="AOTCNovel" />

[[File:XJ-6_hotrod.jpg|thumb|right|270px|Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker race through The Works.]]
Both Skywalker's piloting skills and the vessel's integrity were tested as Wesell led the Jedi into [[The Works/Legends|The Works]], a large industrial area of Coruscant near the [[Senate District/Legends|Senate District]]. Intending to use the lack of protection offered by the XJ-6 airspeeder's open cockpit against her Jedi pursuit, Wesell passed between large smokestacks spewing toxic fumes and [[Fire/Legends|flames]] with the Jedi following closely behind. As a pair of power coupling prongs, sabotaged by a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] bolt from Wesell, began discharging electricity,<ref name="ItWoAotC" /> Skywalker flew through them.<ref name="AotC" /> The XJ-6 was unscathed, attesting to its craftsmanship and ability,<ref name="AotC:ICS" /> but the Jedi piloting the craft were not so fortunate and suffered electrical shocks that, without the assistance of the Force, would have induced [[Heart/Legends|heart]] attacks.<ref name="ItWoAotC" /> The tight passageways and many environmental hazards of The Works took a toll on Skywalker, and he lost control of his maneuvering briefly enough for the airspeeder to graze a number of objects and stall. Skywalker managed to restart the speeder&mdash;now smoking slightly, with flames coming out of the dashboard&mdash;and again pursued the assassin.<ref name="AOTCNovel" />

Once out of The Works, Skywalker left the safer confines of the speeder to confront the assassin by free-falling through the skylanes to land directly on Wesell's airspeeder.<ref name="AotC" /> With Skywalker and Wesell wrestling for control of the assassin's craft, Kenobi took over piloting of the XJ-6 airspeeder and continued to follow the ''Koro''-2. Kenobi tracked Wesell closely enough to catch [[Anakin Skywalker's first lightsaber/Legends|Skywalker's lost lightsaber]], which was thrown from Skywalker's grasp during his struggle.<ref name="AotC" /><ref name="ItWoAotC" /> Eventually, the skirmish between the Padawan and the assassin resulted in a crash-landing. Kenobi circled the crash area before parking the XJ-6 near the [[Outlander Club/Legends|Outlander Club]] on [[Vos Gesal Street/Legends|Vos Gesal Street]].<ref name="HNN" /> Once the Jedi pair reunited, the two proceeded to track the assassin into the Outlander, leaving the XJ-6 parked on the street. Once the Jedi found Wesell amongst the club patrons, they apprehended her. However, before Wesell could be brought back and questioned, her employer,<ref name="AotC" /> the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]]<ref name="SW:UVG:U&E">''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide: Updated and Expanded]]''</ref> [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] hunter [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]], [[Death/Legends|killed]] her.<ref name="AotC" />

===Aftermath===
{{Quote|I never fully trusted that kid. He was always protective and envious of my speeder.|Senator Simon Greyshade, on Reymet Autem, after the latter's arrest|<ref name="HNN" />}}
[[File:XJ6Airspeeder-NEGVV.png|thumb|left|270px|Greyshade never discovered who stole his prized speeder.]]
Coruscanti officials found the vehicle shortly thereafter over 100 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] from its original position in the Senate District. [[Reymet Autem]], son of a [[Sagoro Autem|Senate security guard]] employed by Greyshade, was initially charged with the theft of the speeder. However, before any charges could be filed against the twenty-year-old, the XJ-6 disappeared from the crime scene. It reappeared in the [[Senatorial speeder barn]] at [[500 Republica/Legends|500 Republica]], where Greyshade had a luxurious apartment<ref name="NewFF64" /> and held a designated speeder stall.<ref name="ItWoAotC" /> While [[Coruscant Security Force/Legends|Coruscant Security Force]] [[Officer/Legends|officer]] [[Wets Tranoj]] blamed the premature return on "rookie error,"<ref name="HNN" /> it was actually Skywalker and Kenobi who returned the speeder.<ref name="Databank" />

Greyshade never discovered who had stolen his airspeeder,<ref name="VivaSpaceVegas" /> which left the senator fuming.<ref name="CATCW" /> Sometime later, he relayed the events to Anakin Skywalker at a state dinner. Greyshade vowed that he would find the thief, unaware that the culprit was right in front of him. Skywalker only commented that the speeder must have been taken by a skilled individual to have evaded detection.<ref name="VivaSpaceVegas" /> Though designed as a one-of-a-kind vessel,<ref name="HNN" /> the XJ-6 airspeeder was later mass-produced and made available to [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="SWGalaxies" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Flying in style===
{{Quote|George liked the idea that perhaps some young teenage kid from Coruscant has cooked up this machine. So it has special modifications; that's why you don't see the engine cowlings on there. It's somebody's passion, this little hot rod.|Doug Chiang|<ref name="XJ-6 BTS">{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/bts/design/f20010601/index.html|text=Designs of Ep II: Hot Rod Speeder}}</ref>}}
[[File:XJ-6_Concept.jpg|thumb|right|270px|Concept art of the XJ-6 airspeeder, drawn by Jay Shuster]]
The XJ-6 airspeeder was originally featured on [[StarWars.com]] in [[June]] [[2001]] in a behind-the-scenes article detailing the creation of the speeder as part of the lead up to the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']].<ref name="XJ-6 BTS" /> The XJ-6 made a cameo appearance in the [[December]] 2001 [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']], which featured the speeder on an in-game billboard.<ref name="Obi-Wan Game">[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']]</ref> The speeder later featured in ''Attack of the Clones'' in [[2002]] during the chase scene that began Obi-Wan Kenobi's quest to locate Zam Wesell's employer and Kenobi's eventual discovery of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Republic's clone army]] on the planet [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]].<ref name="AotC" /> The airspeeder's features, including its connection to Senator Simon Greyshade, were first described briefly by the [[April]] 2002 [[Star Wars Visual Dictionaries|reference book]] ''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''.<ref name="AotCVD">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> The [[2003]] book ''[[The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]'' was the first source to provide the airspeeder's designation.<ref name="NEGtVaV" />

===Creating a hot rod===
{{Quote|It didn't take long at all to design. The chosen sketch was done 15-20 minutes before one of the art meetings. There were six or seven drawings on the board, and I had thought 'George is never going to pick this one.' Sure enough, though, you never know what he's going to pick. There was a certain character to it that he enjoyed.|Concept artist Jay Shuster|<ref name="XJ-6 BTS" />}}
Both the XJ-6 airspeeder and the chase through Coruscant, as depicted in ''Attack of the Clones'', were based mostly on ''[[Star Wars]]'' creator [[George Lucas]]'s love of classic vehicles.<ref name="Databank" /> For the pivotal chase scene, a team of art designers was asked to create a hot-rod airspeeder with a distinct style. Concept artist [[Jay Shuster]] created the original design of the XJ-6 airspeeder mere minutes before a meeting to determine the airspeeder's design. Though the decision was unexpected, Lucas chose this design over numerous other choices.<ref name="XJ-6 BTS" />

[[File:XJ6BTS.jpg|thumb|left|270px|The XJ-6 prop on set]]
Shuster supposed that Lucas saw [[Anakin Skywalker's Podracer/Legends|Anakin Skywalker's Podracer]], featured in the [[1999]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], in the design, which influenced his decision.<ref name="ArtOfAOTC">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones]]''</ref> By Lucas's own admission, the speeder also bears a strong resemblance to a car driven by [[Wikipedia:Paul Le Mat|Paul Le Mat's]] character John Milner in Lucas's [[1973]] film, [[Wikipedia:American Graffiti|''American Graffiti'']].<ref name="Commentary">{{Film|II}} [[Star Wars home video releases|DVD]] commentary</ref> Lucas selected the yellow paint scheme minutes after selecting the XJ-6's design; the yellow was chosen because, as Shuster recalled, it mimicked the coloration of the hot rod [[Harrison Ford]]'s character Bob Falfa drove in ''American Graffiti''.<ref name="ArtOfAOTC" /><ref name="ArtOfAOTC-Shuster">According to [[Jay Shuster]] in ''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones]]'', [[George Lucas]] based the yellow paint scheme on the coloration of ''American Graffiti'' character Bob Falfa's hot rod, though Falfa's vehicle was actually colored black in the film.</ref>

Both Shuster and Design Director [[Doug Chiang]] were responsible for many of the final design features of the XJ-6, including the speeder's convertible nature; the exposed, souped-up engines; and even the striking yellow color scheme, intended to make the craft stand out in a [[Standard day/Legends|nighttime]] Coruscant sky. With the basic design chosen, concept modeler [[John Goodson]] created a scale model to further fill out the speeder's details.<ref name="XJ-6 BTS" /> The production model shop team, led by [[Peter Wyborn]], built both the XJ-6 and ''Koro''-2 models for filming. The XJ-6 was then mounted to a set of highly flexible rigging, created by special effects supervisor [[Dave Young]], to recreate the banks and pitch of a craft in flight. Actors [[Ewan McGregor]] and [[Hayden Christensen]], playing Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker, respectively, were filmed interacting with the full-scale model. The two spent hours performing maneuvers as the cameras rolled.<ref name="Mythmaking">''[[Mythmaking: Behind the Scenes of Attack of the Clones]]''</ref> In addition to the realistic model, [[Industrial Light & Magic]] created an extensively detailed computerized version of the speeder to assist in filming.<ref name="XJ-6 BTS" /> Long after filming was complete, sound designers [[Ben Burtt]] and [[Matthew Wood]] developed the distinctive noise of the XJ-6 to be used in the final film.<ref name="Mythmaking" />
